issues.detail: Hebrew 'פַּאֲרֵי פִשְׁתִּים' means 'turbans of linen' (or 'headpieces of linen'), not '榮耀' (glory). The word 'פְּאֵר' is a headdress/turban, not 'glory' (which would be כָּבוֹד). This changes the meaning of the verse.

Hebrew 'בַּיָּזַע' means 'with sweat' (i.e., they shall not gird themselves with sweat, meaning they shall not gird in a way that causes sweat). The Chinese '用汗來纏裹' ('wrap with sweat') is a literal but awkward rendering; however, the main issue is the mistranslation of 'פַּאֲרֵי' as '榮耀'.
